articles.title: How to Find UUFinds QC Photos for the Exact Item You Are Considering
articles.description: Match a marketplace link to a photo set, identify the photographed option, and decide when a new view would answer a real buying question.

sections.heading: Start with the listing you intend to buy
paragraphs: Suppose two black canvas bags appear in your search results. They have the same front pocket and brass zip. One listing offers a short handle, while the other includes a shoulder strap. A photo of the second bag could tell you plenty about its strap clips and very little about what comes with the first. The time to make that distinction is before you start zooming in on stitching. Open the seller page for the bag you actually intend to buy and save the link and selected option together.

The official UUFinds QC Finder describes collecting inspection images from shipping agents. Its search interface accepts several kinds of marketplace links as well as product names. Begin with the original marketplace link if you have it. If you found the bag through a spreadsheet, open its product detail page and use the original listing link there. Keep the spreadsheet tab available so you can return to your chosen option if the marketplace opens a different colour by default.

sections.heading: Make the product ID do the first part of the work
paragraphs: On a Weidian link, look for the number beside itemID. Keep that number together with the marketplace name. A number in the address of a spreadsheet page can refer to the catalogue's own row. Copying that number into another site's search field can send you looking for an entirely different item. If the result shows an original product link, open it and check where it lands. A matching title alone gives you less to go on, especially when a listing title contains only a model name or a broad category.

Some people arrive with a screenshot from a chat and no address at all. In that case, a visually similar result gives you a place to start. Look for two details that narrow the candidate set, such as the shape of the buckle and where the side panel joins the base. Open the promising listings and compare their option menus. Once you identify the seller page you want, carry its link into the QC search and use it for the rest of your review.

sections.heading: Work out which option appears in the photographs
paragraphs: A single listing can hold several products that share a price range or broad description. Before interpreting a photo, write down the selected colour, size and style code exactly as the seller presents them. A translation can make a label easier to read, but the original code lets you recognise the option when another site uses different wording. If a photo shows a label or tag, compare the visible characters with that code. Record any difference precisely enough that you can find it again.

Look for a detail that changes between options on the same page. In the bag example, count the attachment rings or compare the position of the strap keeper. A picture showing the outside of a closed bag may give you a confident colour-family match while leaving the included strap unresolved. If a gallery has no option labels, avoid assigning every photo to the option selected in your browser. Open each relevant image and record which features actually connect it to your choice.

sections.heading: Read a photo set in a useful order
paragraphs: Start with the broadest view. It establishes where the front, back and side panels sit relative to each other and gives context to a close-up. Next look for the reverse side and the base. Those views can reveal an extra pocket, a missing attachment or a different seam layout that the front photograph hides. Only then move to the area that prompted your search. A close-up of a zipper pull becomes easier to interpret when you already know which of two compartments it belongs to.

Judge each image at a scale where the detail remains clear. Phone screens can let you enlarge a small picture until compression makes a normal edge look jagged. If a dark spot appears near a fold, inspect another angle for the same location. A mark that moves with the reflection deserves a different note from a mark that remains on the same piece of fabric across two views. Keep the original image available and save a separate annotated copy if you need to explain what caught your eye.

sections.heading: Separate catalogue pictures from an inspection of a particular piece
paragraphs: A seller's product image can be excellent evidence of what the seller offers. You can use it to identify the advertised fastening, lining colour or included pieces. A warehouse photograph can help you understand how a received piece looked when photographed. On UUFinds Grid, read the section label above the images. A picture in the catalogue gallery remains a reference image even when it looks as though someone took it on a warehouse table. When the page reports that verified QC images are unavailable, keep that distinction in your notes.

A public inspection picture may also belong to someone else's order. Look for any information connecting the image to the listing and the option. Even a good match leaves questions about a different unit purchased later. A straight seam on the photographed bag answers a question about that visible seam. It cannot settle whether a future bag has a working zip or the same finish inside. Use public photos to choose what to examine on your own order if your purchasing service offers an inspection stage.

sections.heading: Decide what a missing view would change
paragraphs: Consider a set that includes the front, back, handles and a size tag. You can count two handles and read the tag. You still cannot see inside the bag. If a laptop sleeve matters to you, the missing interior view is worth following up. If you only need the exterior pocket and its dimensions, an interior photograph adds little. Write the question in a form that someone can answer with one image. A request for the bag open with the inner sleeve and fastening visible gives a clearer instruction than a general request to check the quality.

When a search returns no photos, check the marketplace and item ID one more time. Then note the result against the exact option. An empty search gives you no evidence about workmanship in either direction. You can consult the seller's description, ask the seller about the specific detail, or ask your purchasing provider what a later inspection would cover. Check the current terms in the order interface if an extra photograph or a change to the order matters to your decision.

sections.heading: Keep a record the next person can understand
paragraphs: For a short practical record, keep the source link, selected option, the photo set you used and the date you viewed it. Under those details, write one sentence about what you saw and one about what remains open. For example, the medium navy bag in the set has two visible strap rings and a silver clasp. The pictures stop above the base, so the base width remains open. Someone reading that note next week can see why you shortlisted the item and exactly where to resume.

Before continuing to a purchasing platform, compare the option on its product screen with the note. A new page may open on the first available colour, and a search match can lead to a seller's other listing. If the actual price or available options change, make the decision using what you see in the current order screen. Keep the reference photos and the order confirmation in separate places, so that any later question can be tied to the piece you actually ordered.

sources.title: RepTips — Best QC Photo Finders Compared

articles.title: How to Read QC Measurement Photos Before Choosing a Size
articles.description: Read a ruler image from both endpoints, compare flat garment dimensions with a piece you own, and write a precise request when the evidence is unclear.

sections.heading: Choose a comparison garment before opening the photo
paragraphs: A ruler in a warehouse picture answers a narrow question about one physical piece of clothing. To make that answer useful, find something you own that fits the way you want the new item to fit. Choose a similar shape and material. A loose sweatshirt can be a helpful reference for another relaxed sweatshirt. It tells you much less about the room you want inside a close-fitting woven shirt. Fasten your reference garment the way you would normally wear it and lay it on a level surface.

Write down the one feature you most want to get right. Perhaps the width of your current sweatshirt feels comfortable, while its sleeves ride up when you stretch your arms. In that case take two separate reference measurements. A good chest-width match will still leave the sleeve question open. Keep these figures with the seller's size chart and the source listing. If you take a quick photograph of your own measuring tape in position, you will have an easy visual reference when the warehouse photograph arrives.

sections.heading: Identify the chart and the photographed size
paragraphs: Read the heading on the seller's chart. A body chart describes the person a size is intended to fit, while a product chart may give measurements of the finished garment. The same word, such as chest, can appear in both contexts. UNIQLO's measuring guides illustrate why the distinction matters, including diagrams for measuring clothing laid flat. Use the measuring instructions for the item you are buying when the seller provides them. Different sellers can choose different measuring points for the same broadly named dimension.

Check the product option visible in the QC set. A clearly photographed size label helps tie a measurement to a particular piece. Where a set comes from an earlier public inspection, record the visible size and style. You might be considering an XL while the ruler photo shows a medium. Resist the temptation to add a guessed number of centimetres. If the seller has published a size chart, it can describe the intended difference between sizes, but the photographed width remains a measurement of the sample shown.

sections.heading: Read the two ends before doing any arithmetic
paragraphs: Find the end where the tape meets the first garment edge, then follow the same tape to the second edge. Check the unit and make sure both readings come from the same scale. A tailor's tape can twist so that one end shows a different face. If a hand covers the beginning, or the edge vanishes under the garment, one of the numbers you need is missing. The highest visible number by itself cannot give the distance between two edges.

For example, suppose the tape reads 2 cm at the left seam and 55 cm at the right seam. The distance shown between the seams is 53 cm. That is a worked example, independent of any advertised garment size. A photograph with the zero aligned neatly at the left seam would be easier to read, but the subtraction is valid when both points can be seen clearly. If the right edge falls between two marks and the image is blurry, write down a range that reflects what you can actually read.

sections.heading: Match the route the tape follows
paragraphs: A chest measurement commonly runs across a garment laid flat, but you still need to see where that line starts. A tape drawn from just below one armhole to the other can cross a different part of the garment than a tape placed several centimetres lower. A tapered shirt makes the difference easy to see. Lay your own shirt in the same orientation and measure across the same line. Keep the fabric at rest unless the chart specifically asks for a stretched measurement.

Width and circumference also deserve separate labels in your notebook. When a seller explicitly defines a full measurement as double the flat width, apply that conversion once. A shirt measuring 53 cm across would yield 106 cm under that convention. Leave your comparison in flat widths when both garments have already been measured flat. Doubling a value on only one side can make two almost identical shirts appear wildly different. A printed chest number on a size tag needs its own explanation before you put it in either column.

sections.heading: Adjust your method for sleeves, trousers and elastic
paragraphs: For a set-in sleeve, find where the sleeve joins the shoulder, then identify the cuff edge in the photograph. A raglan sleeve runs towards the neckline and has a different seam layout. A length measured from the neck across the shoulder cannot be compared directly with one starting at a shoulder seam. If the two garments have different construction, choose a route that you can repeat on both, describe that route, and keep the original seller's measurement under a separate heading.

On trousers, trace an inseam from the crotch seam down the inside leg to the hem. A tape following the outside of the leg gives a different dimension because it starts higher. Look for a rolled cuff or a folded waistband before using the number. For an elasticated waist, decide whether your question concerns the resting width or the fabric under tension. If the picture shows someone's hands pulling the waistband apart, it offers little basis for comparison with the resting width of the trousers on your table.

sections.heading: Decide whether the difference matters to you
paragraphs: Imagine your favourite overshirt measures 56 cm across at the agreed points. A clear photo of the proposed size reads 54 cm at the same points. The recorded flat-width difference is 2 cm. Now put on your reference shirt with the layer you plan to wear underneath. Where is there room to spare, and where does it already pull? Your own answer makes the numerical difference more useful than an abstract claim that a garment runs small. The photographs still leave fabric stretch and personal preference to your judgement.

You may find a photo gives a range wide enough to change the decision. If the edge could reasonably sit at either 53 or 55 cm and the difference matters to you, keep that uncertainty visible. Repeating the same estimate at greater zoom will not create a sharper mark. A folded garment, a stretched tape running above the fabric, or a camera pointed across the table can all make it difficult to tell which point aligns with the scale. Name the problem before asking for a replacement shot.

sections.heading: Request one photograph that settles the open question
paragraphs: Use the order or listing reference, colour and size so the recipient can identify the piece. Then describe the placement, endpoints and unit. For instance, ask for the blue medium shirt buttoned and laid flat, with a centimetre tape running straight between the two underarm seams. Request a view that shows both seams and both readings together. If the tag would be unreadable at that distance, a separate label close-up can accompany the full garment view. Check what photo service your actual seller or purchasing provider can offer.

Keep the reply beside your reference photograph and the chart you used. Record the size, unit, route and visible result. If a different seller uses another method later, you can take a fresh measurement of your reference garment along that route without losing the previous comparison. Before checkout or onward shipping, return to the selected colour and size on the live order. This last check connects the time you spent reading a ruler to the particular choice that will actually be processed.

sources.title: UNIQLO — Size Chart and Body / Product Measurement Guide

articles.title: How to buy a UUFinds find through a shopping agent
articles.description: Carry the original item link, exact style and size from a UUFinds find into an agent order, then check the warehouse item before parcel submission.

sections.heading: Start with the item you actually want
paragraphs: A useful test of a UUFinds find is whether you can describe the exact item to someone who has never seen your screen. “The green bag on the second row” only works while the results stay in that order. A marketplace name, item number, seller option and quantity can travel with you all the way to a warehouse inspection. Gather those details before choosing where to buy. The few seconds spent copying them can save a much longer conversation about which item an agent was asked to order.

UUFinds describes its role as helping people browse listings and assess QC photos. The buying decision takes place on a marketplace or through a purchasing service. On UUFinds Grid, open the product page from the spreadsheet and look for the original listing. A link to an image opens a picture; a link to a shop opens a collection. For an order you want the individual product URL. Keep that page open in one tab and use another for your agent so you can check both selections side by side.

sections.heading: Carry the seller's option through the handoff
paragraphs: Suppose a canvas bag comes in olive and black, with short and long straps. The main listing photo can show both colours, and the buying page can use the same picture for both straps. Select the combination you want and write down the seller's option text, even if you keep a translation alongside it. Add the number of units. If you care about an included strap, insert, or box, find the relevant words in the listing. An accessory placed beside the bag in a styled photograph alone leaves the contents of the order unclear.

When the product page supplies a complete SKU, copy the Weidian link and selected option. If the copied text includes a URL followed by a size, style or SKU on separate lines, paste just the URL into the agent's product search. Keep the remaining information for comparison or an order note. Some pages can open at the individual listing while displaying a default option. Look at the highlighted choices after the page opens. A green square beside a photograph means little if the selected option underneath still reads black.

sections.heading: Check the destination of the buying link
paragraphs: You can use a buying-agent link on the product page or paste the original product URL into a service you already use. Superbuy's official shopping-agent guide illustrates how a product link becomes an order with chosen options. Each agent has its own supported sources, interface and policies. A shortcut to a particular service saves typing. Before entering delivery or payment details, read the destination domain and confirm that you have reached the intended service and are signed into the account where you want the order recorded.

Compare the seller name, item ID where available, selected options, unit description and image on the destination page. A translated or shortened title is a weak basis for a decision. If the agent cannot open the original link, check the same listing directly with the marketplace. When the seller page still works, ask the agent which part of the listing it can import or enter manually. When the seller has removed the listing, treat a visually similar result as a fresh purchase decision with its own seller, options and terms.

sections.heading: Read the checkout as an order instruction
paragraphs: Before confirming, read the basket line aloud as if you were the buyer visiting the seller: one olive canvas bag, long strap, quantity one. Check whether the price is per piece or set and whether your selected version changed the amount. For wholesale listings, look for a minimum quantity attached to the offer. Superbuy specifically flags supplier minimums in its guidance for 1688. If you only want a single unit, establish whether the seller offers one at the displayed unit price before funding the purchase.

Look at what the first payment covers. Superbuy's example includes the item and local delivery in China at this stage. If another service combines different charges, follow its itemised summary. Save the order number and the accepted configuration. Someone reading your order later should be able to find the right line without relying on a screenshot of a cart you subsequently edited. If you need to ask a question, include the order number and one concrete question, such as whether the long strap is included with the selected version.

sections.heading: Handle changes while the seller order is open
paragraphs: A seller can run out of one colour while keeping the listing available. Decide how you want to handle that situation before it happens. Someone buying a bag to match existing luggage might prefer a refund to any shade change. Someone who only needs the longer strap might accept a different colour after seeing its photograph and price. If the agent asks about a substitution, compare the proposed option to the original, then record the exact alternative you accept through the order's support channel.

When an order status is unclear, identify what movement you are waiting for. The agent may be waiting for information from you, a response from the seller, or transport to the warehouse. Search the agent account for the specific order before opening a second one for the same product. Creating another paid order because a status has stayed the same can leave you with two purchases. The reference number in your first confirmation is the quickest way to check which transaction an update concerns.

sections.heading: Inspect the warehouse arrival against your own order
paragraphs: QC photographs found during research can help you decide which details deserve a closer look. After purchase, use the images and records attached to your own warehouse item. Start with the visible facts you can compare to your order: colour, shape, strap configuration, count and any readable size or model label. Look at the position of an opening, the number of compartments or the attachment point for a strap. These details often distinguish two versions photographed with the same background and lighting.

Some questions need another view. If the strap length determines whether the bag works for you, request a photograph with the measurement running between the attachment points and the tape visible at both ends. Ask the agent what views it can provide and what they cost before authorising an extra service. If you spot an incorrect option, raise it with the agent while the item is still in its warehouse. Include the relevant photograph, the original order line and the difference you can identify.

sections.heading: Submit the parcel and follow the right reference
paragraphs: After accepting the item, open the parcel or shipping section of the agent account. Select the warehouse item you intend to send, check the destination, and review the options available for its contents and dimensions. If you are combining purchases, count the selected warehouse lines and check that each is ready. If you need the retail box as a gift, make that choice explicitly when reviewing packaging. Taking a box out can change both the protection around the item and how the finished parcel fits its shipping route.

Save the parcel number separately from the seller order number. A question about the wrong strap belongs with the purchase record; a question about the international delivery belongs with the parcel record. At delivery, check the goods against the same short description you saved before buying. That single consistent description connects research, seller selection, warehouse inspection and receipt. It also gives the agent a precise starting point if something in the parcel differs from the order you approved.

articles.title: How to read a UUFinds price, exchange rate and shipping estimate
articles.description: Compare the SKU price, currency conversion and international freight estimate, with worked examples of exchange rates and parcel volume.

sections.heading: Put the price next to the decision it supports
paragraphs: A catalogue price helps you decide whether to open a listing. A price beside a selected size helps you compare two variants. A warehouse parcel quote helps you decide whether you want to send the item by a particular route. Those are three useful numbers collected at different moments. Give each one a place in your notes. Otherwise it is easy to compare a catalogue figure for one item with a checkout figure for another and conclude that the first is a better deal before you have matched what the two offers include.

Start with a short description of the proposed purchase, including quantity, source currency and selected options. If you are comparing a pair of shoes with the same pair in a gift box, make the packaging difference visible in the description. Decide whether your comparison is per pair, per set or per parcel. Then record the amounts you already know beside that description. Leave a blank for anything the seller or agent has yet to quote. A blank keeps an open question visible; entering zero makes the comparison look more certain than it is.

sections.heading: Find the price that applies to your SKU
paragraphs: The catalogue can give you a starting price before a particular size and style are selected. Open the original product and reproduce the intended combination. Check which amount changes when you move between options. A bag sold on its own and a bag bundled with an accessory may share an item ID. A seller can also list several sizes at different prices. Match the option text and sale unit before multiplying by quantity. If an option cannot currently be selected at checkout, use another available offer when estimating the cost of a purchase you can actually make.

Watch the distinction between a price range and a confirmed basket line. A range can tell you which listings are worth examining, yet it says little about the amount due for your chosen version until you select it. Copy both the source amount and its currency alongside the selected SKU. Compare the agent's basket with that entry. If the numbers differ, first check unit count, domestic delivery and the selected version. Only after those agree is it useful to investigate the exchange rate or a fee.

sections.heading: Calculate a conversion in the correct direction
paragraphs: UUFinds Grid uses Frankfurter reference rates for its currency display. Check the date beside the rate when you compare figures, and retain the source-currency amount. A dated reference lets two people compare prices on the same basis even if their payment methods differ. The amount you authorise comes from the seller, agent or payment provider at checkout. If that page quotes a local-currency total, write down the amount it actually asks you to approve and the source amount it says this covers.

Here is an arithmetic example using invented round figures solely to show direction. Suppose a reference quote reads seven yuan per US dollar and a selected item is 140 yuan. Dividing 140 by seven gives a reference value of 20 dollars. If the quote instead reads dollars per yuan, multiply the yuan amount by that figure. Writing the units alongside the calculation makes errors obvious: the yuan units should cancel, leaving dollars. Keep full precision while comparing several items and round the display total at the end.

sections.heading: Separate the item payment from parcel expenses
paragraphs: Create a row for the goods and another for the seller's delivery to the agent. When the agent gives a combined checkout total, mark which rows that total already includes. Add a separate row only for a charge shown separately. For example, a domestic delivery amount printed beneath an item subtotal might already be part of the bold total at the bottom of the page. Adding it to that total a second time quietly overstates the price of the order.

For an estimate of the international stage, record destination, route, package assumptions and any selected services. Options such as reinforcement or changes to packaging should be included at the price quoted by the service when you choose them. Keep any charges listed as payable later in a separate column until you know the amount. When a comparison involves two agents, align the assumptions. One quote with the gift box retained and a second with that box removed answer different questions, even if both display the same currency.

sections.heading: Read the dimensions before comparing shipping routes
paragraphs: A parcel has both scale weight and outside dimensions. A bulky package can occupy considerable transport space while weighing little. Superbuy's estimator explains volumetric weight and illustrates a calculation for air cargo. Read the formula, units, size limits and rounding rules shown for your specific route. A height measured in millimetres entered into a centimetre field will distort the result by a factor of ten even if the other dimensions are correct. Use external packed dimensions where the calculator asks for parcel measurements.

Consider two possible packages for the same soft item. In a worked example, a box measuring 40 by 30 by 20 centimetres occupies 24,000 cubic centimetres. A box measuring 40 by 30 by 12 occupies 14,400. With a hypothetical route divisor of 6,000 cubic centimetres per kilogram, the corresponding volume weights are 4 and 2.4 kilograms. These figures describe the example packages only. Compare the applicable value with the actual packed weight under the chosen route's rules before translating a difference in size into a difference in cost.

sections.heading: Account for the first weight unit and shared parcels
paragraphs: Some estimates split the tariff into a first weight unit and later units. Under such a tariff, two individual parcels can each incur a first-unit charge. A combined parcel may cross another weight step or enter a different size category. Run the actual combinations through the same estimator, then compare the totals. Simply doubling the estimate for one item assumes a straight-line price per kilogram, which may produce the wrong answer for both the two-parcel and one-parcel options.

If you are dividing a combined parcel with another shopper, agree how to allocate its shipping cost. Splitting by item count can be reasonable for several nearly identical shirts, but it gives a misleading impression of individual costs when one box contains a small scarf and another contains a bulky bag. You can instead compare the route estimate with and without the bulky item, or agree to share freight in proportion to an agreed weight measure. Record the method so a later comparison against a single-item purchase remains intelligible.

sections.heading: Reconcile the estimate after packing
paragraphs: Superbuy's guidance describes an international shipping deposit based on the available estimate, with the carrier's verified package measurements used for the final freight calculation. Check the procedure of the agent you actually choose. Save its quote, the deposit and the eventual transaction record separately. When a final adjustment appears, determine whether it changes the charge, returns part of a deposit, or pays for an extra service. Counting the deposit and the whole final freight amount as two separate charges would duplicate a large part of the parcel cost.

Once the parcel journey is complete, add the confirmed payment lines in a common currency. Keep each source-currency amount beside its conversion so the arithmetic can be checked later. Include any separately confirmed destination charge in your own comparison, and label a cost that is still unknown. For your next purchase, the most informative figure is often the difference between the estimated and actual total, together with its cause. A packaging dimension, an unavailable variant and a change in the payment conversion can all move a total in different ways.

articles.title: How to use the UUFinds Chrome extension for product QC photos
articles.description: Find the developer’s Chrome Web Store listing, check the exact product and selected option, and troubleshoot a missing QC album.

sections.heading: Start with the marketplace tab you already have
paragraphs: If you have a Weidian item open on a laptop, the most useful question about the UUFinds browser extension is simple. Can you look for quality-control photos while keeping that exact item in view? That is the use the UUFinds developer describes in the Chrome Web Store. The listing also mentions a website that works with marketplace and agent links. Those are two routes to the same research question. You can start on a product page with the extension, or take its original address to the website and look it up there.

Consider a canvas tote offered in both zip-top and open-top versions. You have already found the zip-top option and want to know how the zip is attached at the corners. Keep the seller tab open on that option before looking for photos. A successful search should give you another view of the relevant bag and enough context to associate it with your item. Finding a handsome photograph of an open-top bag leaves the original question unanswered. Starting with the detail you care about gives the extension a concrete job.

sections.heading: Find the publisher's Chrome Web Store listing
paragraphs: The extension's Web Store title includes several shopping-agent names alongside UUFinds. Check the publisher shown on the listing, uufinds2024, and use the store link in the sources below. Chrome also gives every Web Store extension an identifier. The UUFinds entry ends in fjifkdnhlhndjblobgfjdallikchiape. The publisher and identifier are especially helpful when a search returns reviews, guides, similarly named extensions or pages displaying an installation button of their own. Bookmark the actual store page if you expect to revisit it on another computer.

In desktop Chrome, open that listing and read the current description before choosing Add to Chrome. Chrome presents any necessary permission request as part of its installation flow. Review the wording shown in your own browser and decide whether it suits the task. On a computer managed by a school or employer, installation may be controlled by the administrator. The official UUFinds web page gives you a separate way to carry out a product lookup when installing browser software is inconvenient. A phone user can also start with the website without changing anything on a desktop.

sections.heading: Check the first lookup against a known item
paragraphs: For the first test, pick a marketplace listing with a clear title, a recognizable option and an original product URL. Write down the marketplace and the visible item number. You can record a short description alongside them, such as navy tote, zip top, regular handles. Open the listing in the browser profile where you added the extension. Keeping an unchanged copy of the address in your notes means you can repeat the lookup after following another link, changing the page language or switching agents.

Look for the product-related QC images described by the developer. If a photo area appears, check which listing it identifies and whether it gives an option name, date or order context. Open one view wide enough to see the shape and another close enough to inspect the feature you wrote down. On the tote, that might mean a front view to establish the design and a corner view to see the zip tape. A photo with an unclear connection to the selected option is still useful as a lead. Mark down the uncertainty before treating it as buying evidence.

sections.heading: Understand what “corresponding QC photos” can tell you
paragraphs: A QC image can answer a question about the photographed unit. For example, a clear picture of the inside pocket can show which side carries the zip pull. It tells you much less about how the zip feels, how the stitching will wear or which unit will arrive in a future parcel. This distinction matters on multi-option pages. One seller can list several sizes, colours and constructions under the same product title. Test visible details against the selected option each time you reopen an album.

The Web Store description refers to viewing images while browsing and describes link conversion as part of the wider UUFinds service. It gives no coverage figure for individual listings. If your result has no matching album, write down what the interface actually showed and when you checked. An empty lookup does not establish that the seller has never shipped the item. It also gives you no basis for concluding that the item passed an inspection. You can return to the listing, compare the seller's description and ask for a specific photo if the missing detail matters.

sections.heading: Follow a converted link without losing the original
paragraphs: A marketplace link identifies the underlying listing. An agent link opens a buying service's presentation of a product. The route from one to the other matters when you save a product for later or pass the result to someone using another agent. Before opening a converted link, keep the original marketplace address and the exact option text together. Open the destination separately, then compare the product number where visible, the item name and the available options. Brand wording or a familiar thumbnail alone can leave two closely related models looking identical.

On the tote example, check that the destination offers the zip-top option in navy and that the selected size is the one you recorded. If the destination opens a different default, select the intended option again and review the displayed price and availability. If it only offers the open-top bag, stop at that point and reopen the original link. Your notes now tell you precisely where the two pages diverge. The shopping platform you eventually use is where you should verify the final selection, price and order details before you submit anything.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot a blank result one question at a time
paragraphs: First establish whether Chrome has the extension enabled in the profile where the product is open. The Extensions menu lets you find an installed extension even when its icon is absent from the toolbar. Chrome's management page also exposes site-access settings. Read the current setting and check the site you are visiting. If you decide to grant site access, choose the scope appropriate for your own browsing. Reload the original listing and repeat the same test before making any further changes. Changing machines, products and settings at once makes the result difficult to interpret.

Next, distinguish the page type. A shop homepage, a search-results grid or a shared screenshot may show the right item while lacking the address of its product page. Open the individual product, confirm the item number and try the website lookup with that address. If another known product returns photos while this one stays empty, you have narrowed the issue to the listing or its available photo coverage. If neither route yields evidence, save the link and the missing detail. That is enough to revisit the case without repeatedly changing browser permissions.

sections.heading: Keep a record that survives the browsing session
paragraphs: For a shortlist, save one line per item with marketplace, source URL, chosen option, date checked and the particular detail the photos show. Add the agent link in its own field if you used one. For the canvas tote you might record that the corner view shows stitched zip ends, while the lining colour remains unclear. That short distinction will still make sense next week if the album order changes. Someone helping you can reopen the source listing and look for the same feature without guessing which navy bag you meant.

An occasional check may only need the website. Someone comparing many marketplace tabs on a desktop might prefer the extension because the item remains in view as they look for corresponding photos. Choose whichever route makes it easiest to keep the evidence attached to its source. If the extension is no longer useful, Chrome's extension manager lets you disable or remove it. Your own notes, original links and unanswered questions will remain useful whichever browser or buying platform you use next.

sources.title: UUFinds extension on the Chrome Web Store
Google Chrome Help: Install and manage extensions

articles.title: How to compare QC photos across sellers and duplicate listings
articles.description: Use original product IDs, matched options and comparable views to choose between similar marketplace listings.

sections.heading: Start by deciding whether you have two sellers
paragraphs: Two finds appear next to each other in a spreadsheet. Both show a square black shoulder bag with a silver buckle, and one costs less. Before you compare stitching, open the source links. You may have found two different listings, two colour options on one listing, or two shopping agents displaying the same seller's product. Each case calls for a different decision. Two agent pages for one source item let you compare buying terms. Two distinct source listings give you a reason to look for evidence about what each seller supplied.

Write down the marketplace and item number from each original link. A Weidian address commonly carries the number in its itemID parameter. When the same number appears on two Weidian links, treat them as one listing for the first pass. If a shop name is visible, keep it beside the number. Compare item numbers within their own marketplace, since numbers from different sites belong to different systems. Give each distinct listing a short name, such as Bag A and Bag B, so you can discuss the photos without relying on matching thumbnails.

sections.heading: Agree on the option and the question
paragraphs: Pick a version that both sellers actually offer. Matching a black bag with a detachable strap to a black bag with a sewn-in strap can make one album look wrong when the products simply differ. Open the options and note the seller's labels for colour, size, hardware finish and included pieces. A photo of a model carrying the bag helps you recognize the shape, but a product option stating that the long strap is included is a separate piece of evidence. Record both when the strap is important to you.

Now give the comparison a purpose. Perhaps the bag must hold a particular book, the strap needs to detach, or you prefer a zipper that closes the top completely. Choose two or three questions you genuinely need answered. For the book, you will need compatible measurements and an opening wide enough to use the space. For the strap, a clear view of the attachment may settle the question immediately. A page full of attractive details can otherwise draw your attention away from the one feature that determines whether you will use the bag.

sections.heading: Put each album back beside its source
paragraphs: Search each exact listing separately for QC photos. Picksly describes looking up a marketplace link, seeing albums associated with it and comparing similar goods across sellers. QC Photo Finder explains that its own public photos are matched by listing number. Taking the original link as the starting point preserves the distinction between a seller's catalogue images and an album associated with a previous order. Keep a tab or a note for each source. When the tool labels an image as a warehouse photo, keep that context with the image.

Start your notes with the views available for each listing. One album might show front, back and lining, while another has a single angled photograph. Include an option label or date if the source supplies one. When neither is shown, leave the field empty. Do not assign a size from the title of another tab. A distinctive scratch in the table, the same folds in the bag and an identical crop can also reveal the same image appearing in several places. Count it once when you consider how many separate observations you have.

sections.heading: Compare like views and admit when they differ
paragraphs: Put front views side by side for the overall outline. Use the width of the buckle relative to its own flap, the position of a pocket relative to the seam, or the order of panels as landmarks. Those relationships remain easier to interpret across different camera distances than the apparent width on a screen. Before comparing a corner or strap attachment, check which side faces the camera. A left-side attachment facing away from the lens can look shorter simply because its edge is partly hidden by the bag.

Colour is a particularly poor tiebreaker when the images come from different rooms. Warm light can change how grey hardware looks, while highlights on a curved buckle can hide its finish. Note the actual observation, such as a cooler-looking finish in the front photograph. Leave the underlying material open unless the source supplies better evidence. Likewise, a tall bag stuffed with packing paper and a similar bag photographed flat can look like different sizes. Seek a tape or dimensions tied to the relevant option before treating the apparent size difference as decisive.

sections.heading: A worked example with two black shoulder bags
paragraphs: Imagine Seller A has a clear rear view and an inside view. The black option shows a removable strap clipped to metal rings. Seller B offers a black option at a lower displayed item price, but its album shows a brown bag from the front and the seller's black studio shot from above. For a shopper who needs to detach the strap, A has direct photographic support for that feature. B remains a plausible option. The available pictures simply leave the attachment on its black version outside the frame.

The sensible follow-up for B is very small. Ask whether the black option includes the long strap and whether a photo can show its fastening at the side of the bag. You need neither another glamour shot nor a general statement that the quality is good. If the seller provides a labelled side view, add that specific image to B's record and revisit the decision. If the answer stays vague, you can choose A on the strength of a visible feature or postpone the purchase. Neither choice requires a general verdict about which shop makes better bags.

sections.heading: Treat old photos and replacement listings carefully
paragraphs: An old album can be useful when its option and construction still match what is on sale. Look for details that identify the version you want, such as the number of interior pockets or a new shape of strap clip. When a newer seller page shows a different arrangement, write down the discrepancy alongside the date. QC Photo Finder notes that names and goods behind a listing can change. An item number is a strong way to organize evidence, yet the current listing still needs to agree with the photos.

A relisted item creates the opposite problem. The shop may present a familiar design at a new URL while the QC records sit under the old number. Keep the historic album labelled with its original ID. A shop name, thumbnail and title shared by both pages establish a lead for further investigation. They leave the present option, material and supplied accessories unresolved. Ask a seller about the change or wait for a clearer record under the new listing if one of those details affects the purchase. Preserve the old link for reference without silently moving its evidence to the new item.

sections.heading: Make a choice another person could reproduce
paragraphs: Finish by writing a few sentences that another shopper can check against the same pages. A useful note names the option, the feature and the view. For example, the rear view of A's black bag shows the lower strap clips, while the opening width is unknown for both. Add the date and original link for each listing. Keeping the outstanding question beside the favourable observation makes it easier to stop searching when you have enough evidence and to ask a precise question when you do not.

Only compare the price after matching the contents of the offers. A bag sold alone and a bag bundled with a pouch can have different prices for a perfectly ordinary reason. Check the current option and buying terms on the destination page before deciding whether the difference matters. Once your order arrives, inspect that individual unit through the process offered by your buying platform. Your earlier comparison explains why you chose a listing. The photos of the unit assigned to your order give you the information you need for the next decision.

sources.title: Picksly: QC checker for marketplace listings
QC Photo Finder: How listing numbers and warehouse photos are matched

faq.question: What can I do with the UUFinds spreadsheet?
faq.answer: Browse product cards by category, search a name or source ID, and open a product to inspect photos, options and buying links. Use the page selector to move farther through the catalogue. To place an order, continue to the seller or buying platform shown on the product page.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: How do I find QC photos for a specific Weidian item?
faq.answer: Open the original Weidian listing and copy its full product URL. Try that link in the official UUFinds QC Finder. Compare the returned item number and any visible style or size with your selection. If no photo identifies the option, its appearance still needs confirmation.

faq.question: Can I use a screenshot to find a product?
faq.answer: Open the camera beside the search field and choose an image from your device. Crop a screenshot down to one item before selecting it, especially if it includes a chat window, several product tiles or large captions. Then compare matching cards with the original screenshot.

faq.question: How do I copy a Weidian link for the exact style and size?
faq.answer: Open a product, select the style and complete the remaining options. When the selection resolves to one listed variant, the selection summary shows its SKU. Use the copy button and keep the accompanying style and size text. After opening the link, check which options the seller page actually selected.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Does the price in my currency include shipping?
faq.answer: The currency selector converts the displayed item price using a reference exchange rate. Shipping, taxes and platform fees are separate. Open the same style and size on your chosen platform and use its order summary or shipping estimate for the amounts charged there.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Why are catalogue photos and QC photos shown separately?
faq.answer: A catalogue image helps identify a listing or choose a style. A warehouse inspection photo can show details of a particular item that someone received. Check the photo label and any visible option information before using the image as evidence about a particular order.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Why can a product have plenty of photos but no verified QC images?
faq.answer: A listing may supply a full gallery and several style thumbnails even when the catalogue has no identified warehouse photos for that item. Follow the original product link to check its identity, then try the official QC finder. An empty QC section alone tells you little about quality.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Which pictures does UUFinds Grid image search compare?
faq.answer: The image index includes source product pictures, gallery photos and indexed style images. A matching style thumbnail can therefore lead to a product whose cover looks different. Open the match and inspect its style selector to find the image you recognized.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Which image should I choose if my photo is rejected?
faq.answer: Try a JPG, PNG or WebP your browser can open and keep the file at or below 20 MB. For a very large camera photo, save a smaller copy cropped around the item. Retain the labels, seams or pattern that help distinguish the model.

faq.question: Where does my image go when I use visual search?
faq.answer: Your browser processes the selected photo on your device. It loads the catalogue image index to calculate visual matches. The first search can take longer while those files arrive. Keep the search tab open until the results or a status message appears.

faq.question: Can a visual match tell me which seller supplied my item?
faq.answer: Use a match as a lead. Two sellers can show the same photo, and one listing can contain several similar colourways. Open the candidates and compare their original links, item numbers and style labels. If you already have the source link, use its item number to identify the listing.

faq.question: What is the difference between a Weidian item ID and a SKU?
faq.answer: The item ID identifies the listing. Its SKU identifies one combination of options within that listing. For example, the Grid page for Weidian item 7880141682 lists several style codes. Customers choosing different styles or sizes can share an item ID but need different SKUs.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Why does my Grid product URL show a shorter number than Weidian?
faq.answer: Grid uses a catalogue page address and displays the original marketplace ID inside the page. For the example ending in /shoes/3475.html, the Weidian item ID is 7880141682. Copy the source link from the page when sharing the item with a buying agent.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Which part of a Taobao or 1688 link should I keep for a QC lookup?
faq.answer: Keep the marketplace and the original product number together. A Taobao item link may contain id= followed by the number. A 1688 offer link may show it between /offer/ and .html. Copy the full product address into the official finder so the platform and product remain identifiable.

faq.question: How can I compare lower-priced shoes without scrolling every category?
faq.answer: Choose Shoes in the spreadsheet, then select the price sort to show lower item prices first. Check the currency selector before comparing two cards. Open any promising product and choose your actual size and style to see the applicable option price when available.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: How do I get back to a page deep in the spreadsheet?
faq.answer: Scroll to the page controls below the product cards. Enter a page number within the displayed range and use Open. The address keeps your category, keyword and sort settings, so you can bookmark that view. A changing catalogue can move a particular item to another page later.

faq.question: What should I try when a product name returns no results?
faq.answer: Clear any category filter, then search one distinctive word from the original title or try the source item ID. A translated title or an agent’s rewritten product name may differ from the catalogue text. If the spelling is uncertain but you have a clear photo, try image search.

faq.question: Why does the price change after I pick a size or colour?
faq.answer: The product card shows the catalogue price. Selecting a style can narrow the applicable variants, and a complete selection can have a different source price. Check the selected style, size, currency and reference price on the detail page before comparing it with the seller’s current listing.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Can I use a ruler in a QC photo to decide whether a size fits?
faq.answer: Use the dimension you can actually read. For a top, check whether the tape runs across the laid-flat chest or all the way around it. Measure a garment you already wear the same way. A cropped tape endpoint or an unknown size label leaves the comparison incomplete.

faq.question: How do I open the same item on another buying platform?
faq.answer: Expand Other buying agents on the product page and choose the platform you want. The destination may ask you to sign in or select options again. Compare the source ID, item photo, size and price there before adding the item to a cart.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: What does a disabled size mean after I select a style?
faq.answer: The current option data does not offer an available combination for that size and the other choices you have made. Try another style or return to the original listing to check current stock. A size that appears under one colour may be unavailable under another.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices

faq.question: Where do I register for an official UUFinds account?
faq.answer: Use the Register link in the site header. It opens the registration page on www.uufinds.com. If you only want to look up an item, you can browse the Grid spreadsheet and open product pages before deciding whether you need an official account.

faq.question: Do I need the UUFinds Chrome extension to use the spreadsheet?
faq.answer: You can browse the Grid catalogue and use its camera search directly on the website. The separate UUFinds extension is listed in the Chrome Web Store for shoppers who want to check available QC pictures while browsing supported product pages. Check the developer name uufinds2024 in the store.

sources.title: UUFinds extension in the Chrome Web Store

faq.question: Why do model codes stay the same when I switch languages?
faq.answer: A style label such as DMXC-01 is an identifier you can compare with the original listing. Keep it exactly as shown when sharing the item. Use the language menu for navigation and descriptions, and check the numeric item ID or SKU when names differ across sites.

sources.title: UUFinds Grid product options and prices
